newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Intel opens plant in Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Intel opens plant in Philippines.

text.p: Semiconductor firm Intel Corp has opened a plant in the Philippines which officials said was the firm's largest such facility in Asia.
The assembly plant is part of an Intel investment plan under which it will spend a total of 23.4 billion pesos over a five-year period ending year 2001, they said.

"This new facility will assemble and test the Pentium family of processors and later on, the succeeding generations of the most advanced, state-of-the-art Intel microprocessors," Intel Philippines general manager Jacob Pena said during the plant's inauguration in Cavite, south of Manila.

The Cavite test and assembly plant has a total floor area of 600,000 square feet, making it the largest of Intel plants in Asia. The company has begun building a 200,000 square feet plant just across the first plant, officials said.
Company officials said the physical size of the plant made it the largest in Asia but they declined to give production figures.
Intel's Asia-Pacific operation also assembles microprocessing chips in Malaysia and China.
Intel Technology and Manufacturing Group vice president Ken Thompson said the company has decided to expand its operation in the Philippines due to the large pool of skilled workers.
President Fidel Ramos, who led the inauguration ceremonies, urged local and multinational companies to put the Philippines among the top manufacturers of information technology products.
